violations.why: closer1_isr (prio 2) reads var1 twice. writer1_isr (prio 4) can preempt between the reads and write var1, so the two reads can see different values.
writer3_isr (prio 1) writes array[TRIGGER] and later reads it. closer3_isr (prio 4) can preempt in between and overwrite it with 999.
closer1_isr sets expect_close to 42 and later reads it. writer1_isr (prio 4) can preempt and reset it to 0, so the check at 1017 no longer sees 42.
writer2_isr (prio 4) can preempt closer1_isr and overwrite expect_close between its write and read.
closer1_isr sets count to 1 and then tests it. writer1_isr can preempt and set it to 0, so the branch is skipped.
closer2_isr (prio 2) writes expect_close and later reads it. writer1_isr (prio 4) can preempt in between and overwrite it.
writer1_isr writes count=0 and then tests it. closer3_isr (prio 4, equal priority) can preempt and set count=1, so the test sees a different value.
